focus: Conversations: how a terminal chat with a bot and its memory could reuse the bots CLI, run records and needs-you resume path, and which repos ship a terminal UI or conversation shell worth copying.
noveltyJustification: 7 of 8 findings were fully new and 1 synthesized the four app surfaces onto existing stores.
ruledOut: Reusing the existing headless run path unchanged for chat

label: OpenBot's conversation is where work is given and reported, can hold more than one Bot, and each Bot takes the part of the work that is its job.
A conversation creates a channel and an Intelligence thread, two conversations with the same Bot stay separate, and a Bot's standing role is sent with every run so the job need not be restated.
Skilled bots' run path is explicitly headless: one run is one headless executor invocation, and the prompt tells the child that nobody is at a prompt and no answer can reach it.
The bots CLI has no chat or conversation verb; its verbs are run, disable, enable, pause, resume, inbox, enqueue, drain, schedule, answer and status.
Turnstone ships a real terminal front end: TerminalUI implementing a SessionUI protocol, readline setup, model auto-detection, workstream management and a REPL entry point, under Apache-2.0.

openhuman ships openhuman-tui, a conversation-first ratatui terminal frontend covering login, saved conversations, model and agent selection, approvals, tools, child-run inspection and diagnostics; it is GPL-3.0, so design reference only.

The smallest terminal conversation is a bots chat verb keeping an append-only conversation JSONL under the state root, sending the BOT.md body as the standing role, and dispatching one headless run per user message with the transcript; several bots need only a botId per message plus @bot routing. Size M, medium risk.

A TUI can carry all four app surfaces from existing data: conversation over the new file, approvals over bots inbox, activity over the status index, and routines over the BOT.md trigger plus schedule state; a desktop shell adds notifications, tray, hotkey, embedded browser and auto-update, none required for the information model.
